questions.question_text: In which theory is the acid an electron pair acceptor and the base an electron pair donor ?

options.D: Hard and Soft acid base concept

questions.explanation: The Lewis theory defines acids as electron pair acceptors and bases as electron pair donors.

questions.question_text: Muriatic acid is the synonym of
questions.explanation: Muriatic acid is the historical and industrial synonym for hydrochloric acid.

questions.question_text: 2% W/V iodine and 2.5% W/V Potassium Iodide
questions.explanation: Weak iodine solution (iodine tincture or Lugol's relative formulations depending on vehicle) contains 2% w/v iodine and 2.4-2.5% w/v potassium iodide.

questions.question_text: Astringent compound exhibit the following properties except :
questions.explanation: Astringents act locally to precipitate proteins, exhibiting styptic, anti-inflammatory, and antiperspirant properties, but not antitussive properties.

questions.question_text: Flower of sulphur is the synonym of
questions.explanation: Sublimed sulfur is commonly known as flowers of sulfur.

questions.question_text: Chlorine reacts with Calcium Hydroxide to produce
questions.explanation: Reaction of chlorine gas with calcium hydroxide yields chlorinated lime (bleaching powder).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not used as expectorant ?
questions.explanation: Sodium nitrite is a vasodilator and antidote for cyanide poisoning, whereas the others are recognized expectorants.

questions.question_text: In the assay of Hydrogen Peroxide the indicator used is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide assay is a permanganometric redox titration where potassium permanganate acts as both titrant and self-indicator.

questions.question_text: Drugs that help in removing sputum from respiratory tract either by increasing fluidity of sputum or increasing the volume of fluid that have to be expelled from respiratory tract
questions.explanation: Expectorants facilitate the removal of bronchial secretions by decreasing viscosity or increasing volume.

questions.question_text: The assay of Calcium Gluconate is conducted by which titration method ?
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate is typically assayed using complexometric titration with disodium EDTA.

questions.question_text: The sterilization technique in which the final container is heated at $80 \ ^\circ\text{C}$ for one hour on each of three successive days
questions.explanation: Tyndallization involves intermittent heating (often around 80-100 degrees Celsius) on successive days to kill bacterial spores.

questions.question_text: Unequal distribution of colour on a coloured tablet is known
questions.explanation: Mottling refers to an unequal distribution of color on the surface of a tablet.

questions.question_text: In hot air oven the heat is transferred from source to the article by
questions.explanation: Heat transfer in a hot air oven involves a combination of conduction, convection, and radiation.

questions.question_text: The following compounds are used as binders and adhesives except :
questions.explanation: Stearic acid is commonly used as a lubricant or glidant, not as a binder or adhesive.

questions.question_text: Capsules that do not disintegrate in the stomach but break up in the intestine are known as
questions.explanation: Enteric-coated capsules resist gastric fluid and release their active ingredients in the intestine.

questions.question_text: All the gases given below are used for gaseous sterilization except
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide is an anesthetic gas and propellant, whereas the others are well-known sterilizing gases/vapors.

questions.question_text: The hygroscopic or eutectic substance that can be filled into hard gelatine capsules as adsorbent are
questions.explanation: Magnesium oxides, calcium carbonates, and kaolin can all serve as adsorbents for hygroscopic or eutectic mixtures in hard gelatin capsules.

questions.question_text: In hard gelatine capsule the approximate capacity in mg of capsule number "0" is
questions.explanation: A size "0" hard gelatin capsule has an approximate capacity of 680 mg (commonly cited around 650 mg depending on powder bulk density).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not used as enteric coating materials ?
questions.explanation: Gelatin is soluble in the stomach and is used for capsule shells, not as an enteric coating.

questions.question_text: In sterilization the time required at a given condition to achieve log reduction that is to kill 90 percent of organism is called
questions.explanation: D-value (decimal reduction time) is the time required to reduce the microbial population by 90% (1 log reduction) at a specific temperature.

questions.question_text: Irregular lumps in which modular masses are embedded is the microscopic character of
questions.explanation: Socotrine aloe powder exhibits irregular fragments in which yellowish-brown modular masses are embedded under the microscope.

questions.question_text: Purgative action of aloe is due to
questions.explanation: The primary active purgative constituent of aloe is aloin (barbaloin).

questions.question_text: Legal test is the identification test for
questions.explanation: Legal test is used for identifying certain glycosides, specifically C-glycosides found in Aloe.

questions.question_text: Saffrole is the chemical constituent present in
questions.explanation: Safrole is a phenylpropene derivative found naturally in nutmeg and mace.

questions.question_text: Chemical constituent of Nuxvomica which is a dog poison
questions.explanation: Strychnine is an extremely toxic alkaloid from Nux vomica historically known as a dog poison.

questions.question_text: Hydnocarpus oil is the synonym of
questions.explanation: Hydnocarpus oil is also known as chaulmoogra oil.

questions.question_text: The water soluble chemical constituent of ergot is
questions.explanation: Ergometrine (ergonovine) is water-soluble, unlike most other ergot alkaloids which are water-insoluble.

questions.question_text: Azadirachtin is the chemical constituent present in Neem act as
questions.explanation: Azadirachtin from neem is primarily known for its potent insect antifeedant and growth-disrupting properties.

questions.question_text: Which is used in cheese manufacturing as a substitute of rennin ?
questions.explanation: Papain and other plant proteases like microbial proteases are sometimes utilized as rennet substitutes in cheese making.

questions.question_text: Vitamin A can be synthesized from
questions.explanation: Lemon grass oil contains citral, which serves as a starting material for the industrial synthesis of vitamin A.

questions.question_text: Coalescence of the dispersed globules and separation of the disperse as a separate layer in an emulsion is called
questions.explanation: Cracking (or coalescence) is the irreversible breaking of an emulsion where dispersed globules separate into a distinct layer.

questions.question_text: An example of ointment prepared by chemical reaction method
questions.explanation: Ointment of sulfur (specifically precipitated sulfur ointment) involves a chemical reaction or special trituration, but sulfur ointment USP is prepared incorporating precipitated sulfur.

questions.question_text: Abrasive agent used in dentifrices
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate is a standard abrasive agent widely used in toothpastes and dentifrices.

questions.question_text: Antioxidant used in lipsticks
questions.explanation: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is a common phenolic antioxidant used to prevent rancidity in cosmetic products containing fats and oils.

questions.question_text: Non-aqueous oily vehicle used in parenteral depot formulations ?
questions.explanation: Arachis oil (peanut oil) is a commonly used non-aqueous oily vehicle for intramuscular depot injections.

questions.question_text: Test which is used to ensure parenteral product is free from foreign particles
questions.explanation: The clarity test is performed visually or instrumentally to ensure parenteral solutions are free from suspended foreign particles.

questions.question_text: Percentage w/v of Benzalkonium chloride in eye drop used as preservative
questions.explanation: Benzalkonium chloride is typically used in ophthalmic preparations as a preservative at a concentration of 0.01% to 0.02% w/v.

questions.question_text: Hair removed by chemical method is known as
questions.explanation: Depilation refers to the chemical or physical removal of hair from the skin surface, whereas epilation removes hair from the root.

questions.question_text: Which is the pyrogen test for parenteral product ?
questions.explanation: The Limulus amoebocyte lysate (LAL) test is an in vitro assay used to detect bacterial endotoxins (pyrogens).

questions.question_text: Lyophilisation is the another name of
questions.explanation: Lyophilisation is synonymous with freeze-drying, a dehydration process typically used to preserve labile materials.

questions.question_text: The chemical nature of the antineoplastic drug cisplatin is
questions.explanation: Cisplatin is an inorganic platinum-based antineoplastic coordination complex with the cis configuration of diamminedichloroplatinum(II).

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of Ethacrynic acid as loop diuretic is due to

options.C: the presence of $\alpha, \beta$ – unsaturated ketone forming covalent bond with sulfhydryl groups

questions.explanation: Ethacrynic acid possesses an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone group (an activated double bond) that undergoes Michael addition with sulfhydryl groups of transport proteins.

questions.question_text: Identify the antiparkinsonian drug
questions.explanation: Biperiden is a centrally acting anticholinergic agent used as an antiparkinsonian drug.

questions.question_text: Identify the antidote for cholinesterase inhibitors
questions.explanation: Pralidoxime (2-PAM) is a cholinesterase reactivator used as an antidote for organophosphate poisoning.

questions.question_text: IUPAC name for Salbutamol
questions.explanation: Salbutamol (albuterol) IUPAC name is 4-[2-(tert-butylamino)-1-hydroxyethyl]-2-(hydroxymethyl)phenol.

questions.question_text: Haloperidol – A tranquilizer belong to which class of drugs ?
questions.explanation: Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic drug belonging to the butyrophenone chemical class.

questions.question_text: Penicillin V is also known as
questions.explanation: Penicillin V is biosynthetically or semisynthetically known as phenoxymethylpenicillin.

questions.question_text: Identify an antitubercular drug which is chemically an aliphatic diamine.
questions.explanation: Ethambutol is an oral chemotherapeutic agent that is classified chemically as an aliphatic diamine derivative.

questions.question_text: The antibiotic obtained from Streptomyces venezuelae
questions.explanation: Chloramphenicol was originally isolated from the soil bacterium Streptomyces venezuelae.

questions.question_text: Co-trimoxazole contains two antibiotics. What are they ?
questions.explanation: Co-trimoxazole is a fixed-dose combination of sulphamethoxazole and trimethoprim in a 5:1 ratio.

questions.question_text: Identify the barbiturate used as general anaesthetic.
questions.explanation: Methohexital is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate commonly used for intravenous induction of general anesthesia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used in obstetrical pain ?
questions.explanation: Pethidine (meperidine) has traditionally been preferred over morphine in obstetrics because it causes less neonatal respiratory depression and uterine contraction interference.

questions.question_text: Identify the method of metabolism of salicylates in our body.
questions.explanation: Salicylates are primarily metabolized via conjugation with glycine (forming salicyluric acid) and with glucuronic acid.

questions.question_text: Drug of choice for trigeminal neuralgia.
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is established as the primary drug of choice for the medical management of trigeminal neuralgia.

questions.question_text: These compounds inhibit the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin into adrenergic neurons. What are they ?
questions.explanation: Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) exert their pharmacological activity largely by inhibiting the neuronal reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin.

questions.question_text: Drug used in the diagnosis of Myasthenia gravis
questions.explanation: Edrophonium is a very short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used in the Tensilon test to diagnose myasthenia gravis.

questions.question_text: Identify the calcium channel blocker.
questions.explanation: Verapamil is a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used for hypertension, angina, and supraventricular arrhythmias.

questions.question_text: Loop diuretics act as
questions.explanation: Loop diuretics inhibit the $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+/2\text{Cl}^-$ cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.

questions.question_text: The following is not an antifungal drug :
questions.explanation: Neomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic, whereas Amphotericin-B, Clotrimazole, and Terbinafine are antifungals.

questions.question_text: Oral hypoglycaemic agent causing lactic acidosis as most serious complication
questions.explanation: Phenformin is a biguanide that was largely withdrawn due to a high incidence of fatal lactic acidosis.

questions.question_text: Schedule M1 deals with the requirements of factory premises for the manufacturing of
questions.explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, Schedule M1 specifies the factory premises requirements for manufacturing homeopathic preparations.

questions.question_text: A license to sell stock and exhibit or offer for sale of distribute drugs specified in schedule C1 shall be issued in form
questions.explanation: Form 21A is issued for a license to sell, stock, exhibit, or offer for sale or distribute drugs specified in Schedule C1.

questions.question_text: The drug Clofazimine comes under schedule
questions.explanation: Clofazimine is an anti-leprosy drug that falls under Schedule H of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules.

questions.question_text: The place where the licensee employ the services of a qualified person but drugs are not compounded are called
questions.explanation: A chemist and druggist establishment employs a qualified person to sell drugs without compounding them on-site.

questions.question_text: The ER 1991 prescribes practical training for registration of pharmacist is
questions.explanation: The Education Regulations 1991 (ER 1991) prescribes 500 hours of practical training spread over not less than three months.

questions.question_text: Pharmacy inspectors are appointed by
questions.explanation: Pharmacy inspectors are appointed by the State Government under the provisions of the Pharmacy Act, 1948.

questions.question_text: Who among the given is not the common member of PCI and DTAB ?
questions.explanation: Director CDRI is not typically a statutory common member of both the Pharmacy Council of India and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board.

questions.question_text: The schedule of drugs and magic remedies act 1954 includes which of the following diseases ?
questions.explanation: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act lists numerous prohibited conditions including dropsy, diabetes, and Bright's disease.

questions.question_text: Example of narcotic drug
questions.explanation: Poppy straw, cannabis resin, and coca leaves with ecgonine are narcotics, while the listed options (such as plain poppy seeds or leaves without tops/ecgonine) are typically excluded or exempted.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a psychotropic substance ?
questions.explanation: Mazindol, methyprylon, and pentazocine are all controlled substances classified under psychotropic schedules.

questions.question_text: Which of the following method is used for sales promotion ?
questions.explanation: Coupons, trade stamps, and free samples are all common promotional tools used in marketing and pharmaceutical sales.

questions.question_text: B category items represent which of the following money value ?
questions.explanation: In ABC inventory analysis, category B items typically account for an intermediate value of about 15-20% of total inventory cost.

questions.question_text: A method of recording store balances after every receipt and issue to facilitate regular checking and to obviate closing down stock taking
questions.explanation: Perpetual inventory control is a continuous system of recording inventory balances after every transaction to eliminate the need for a total shutdown stock take.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are essential qualities of a salesman ?
questions.explanation: An effective salesman requires a combination of moral integrity, mental aptitude, and vocational training/skills.

questions.question_text: The scrap which can be anticipated during manufacturing is called
questions.explanation: Legitimate (or normal) scrap is that which is expected and can be anticipated during standard manufacturing processes.

questions.question_text: Mixed bank is a combination of
questions.explanation: A mixed bank combines the functions of commercial banking and industrial banking (financing industries).

questions.question_text: Given in the following are the sources of primary data except :
questions.explanation: Trade associations usually publish secondary reports or aggregated statistics, whereas consumers, salesmen, and dealers provide direct primary data.

questions.question_text: The minimum area required to open a wholesale drugstore is
questions.explanation: According to the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules in India, a minimum area of 10 sq. meters (approximately 108 sq. ft.) is required for a wholesale drugstore.

questions.question_text: The tender issued only in those cases where an item of a proprietary nature or where repetitive order is to be issued in short period
questions.explanation: A single tender is issued for proprietary items or urgent repetitive orders where only one specific supplier is approached.

questions.question_text: Creditorship securities which provide funds to the company on loan basis rather than capital basis is called
questions.explanation: Debentures represent debt instruments or creditorship securities that provide loan capital to a company.

questions.question_text: According to Indian Pharmacopoeia, the storage condition : “Store in refrigerator” means store between :
questions.explanation: Storage in a refrigerator according to the Indian Pharmacopoeia is defined as maintaining a temperature between 2°C and 8°C.

questions.question_text: What is the principle of Limulus Amoebocyte Lysate (LAL) test for pyrogen ?
questions.explanation: The LAL test relies on the enzymatic coagulation of amoebocyte lysate by bacterial endotoxins.

questions.question_text: Who is the secretary of the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee (PTC) ?
questions.explanation: The chief pharmacist typically serves as the secretary of the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee in hospitals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following glass container has high hydrolytic resistance and a high thermal shock resistance ?
questions.explanation: Type I glass is borosilicate glass, which possesses high hydrolytic resistance and excellent thermal shock resistance.

questions.question_text: Choose the incorrect statements about HEPA filter :

options.A: It is useful for the preparation of parenteral product.
options.B: It has the efficiency of removing 100% of particles of 0.3 mcm or larger.
options.C: It is generally described as high-efficiency particulate air filter.

questions.explanation: HEPA filters have a nominal removal efficiency of 99.97% (not 100%) for particles of 0.3 micrometers, making option B the technically incorrect statement.

questions.question_text: The word “Ambulatory care” means
questions.explanation: Ambulatory care refers to medical services provided on an outpatient basis, allowing patients to walk in and out without overnight hospitalization.

questions.question_text: The time taken between placing of an order and receipt of items is known as
questions.explanation: Lead time is defined as the total latency or time elapsed between placing a purchase order and receiving the delivered items.

questions.question_text: Which of the following criteria should be taken into consideration for entry or deletion of drugs in Hospital formulary ?

options.A: The manufacturer of drug should have the license under Drug and Cosmetic Rules.
options.B: The drug must be recognized by Pharmacopoeia.
options.C: The drug should not have secret composition.

questions.explanation: All listed criteria are essential standards and regulatory requirements for including a drug in a hospital formulary.

questions.question_text: The appropriate pH range for ophthalmic preparations is
questions.explanation: The normal pH of tear fluid is around 7.4, and ophthalmic preparations generally aim for a physiological pH range between 6.5 and 8.5 to minimize irritation.

questions.question_text: The process that eliminates many or all pathogenic micro-organisms, except bacterial spores, on inanimate objects is known as
questions.explanation: Disinfection is defined as the process of destroying pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects, excluding bacterial endospores.

questions.question_text: Drug-induced fatal malformations are more if the drugs given in which of the following weeks of pregnancy ?
questions.explanation: The period of organogenesis, which spans from the 3rd to the 11th week of pregnancy, is the time of highest susceptibility to major structural malformations.

questions.question_text: Red blood cell destruction can be triggered in individuals with Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency by the following drugs except :
questions.explanation: Diphenhydramine does not cause hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients, whereas sulfonamides, quinine, and nalidixic acid are known oxidative triggers.

questions.question_text: What are adverse drug reactions (ADRs) ?

options.A: The noxious and unintended effect of drugs which occurs at normal doses.
options.B: The synergistic effects that are seen when some drugs are administered concurrently.
options.C: Harmful chemical interactions between two drugs that are used to treat the same clinical symptoms.
options.D: Responses to increased drug doses required to achieve the same physiological outcome.

questions.explanation: By definition, an adverse drug reaction is a noxious and unintended response to a medicinal product occurring at doses normally used in humans.

questions.question_text: Which of the following agents is an opioid antagonist ?
questions.explanation: Naloxone is a competitive opioid receptor antagonist used primarily to reverse opioid overdose.

questions.question_text: Which route of drug administration is most likely to undergo first-pass effect ?
questions.explanation: Oral administration subjects drugs to hepatic first-pass metabolism before reaching the systemic circulation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is used as an antidote in organophosphorus poisoning ?
questions.explanation: Atropine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist widely used to treat the excessive cholinergic symptoms of organophosphate poisoning.

questions.question_text: What is the normal fasting blood sugar level range ?
questions.explanation: A normal fasting blood glucose level is typically between 70 mg/dL and 100 mg/dL.

questions.question_text: The following food stuffs can cause hypertensive crisis during non-selective Mono Amino Oxidase (MAO) inhibitor therapy :
questions.explanation: Aged cheeses, red wines, and certain chocolates contain tyramine, which can precipitate a severe hypertensive crisis when combined with MAO inhibitors.

questions.question_text: The following are the signs and symptoms of tuberculosis excepts :
questions.explanation: Morning stiffness is a classic sign of inflammatory joint diseases like rheumatoid arthritis rather than tuberculosis.

questions.question_text: The World Health Organization (WHO) programme for International Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring is a worldwide collaboration of more than 150 countries whose aims are the safer use of medicines for patients everywhere and building a global culture of patient safety. The monitoring centre is situated at
questions.explanation: The WHO Collaborating Centre for International Drug Monitoring (the Uppsala Monitoring Centre) is located in Uppsala, Sweden.
